- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and price is rising, model often overreacts; cap upward momentum at 1–2% above recent peak.
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon; apply a 1–3% upward bias for 10–15 day forecasts if sentiment is bullish.
- Model overestimates downward moves in the 20+ day horizon; reduce forecast by 0.5–2% for 20+ day periods if sentiment is bearish.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.6 to -0.4 within 3 days), model fails to adjust; apply a 1–2% downward correction to forecast 3–7 days ahead.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to overshoot; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-stage rallies; add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment if sentiment is positive and price is trending upward.
